candidates.exact_span: The permittee must report total or total recoverable metal concentrations for compliance purpose.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether compliance is measured and compared against limits using total/total recoverable versus dissolved concentrations affects which numeric limit applies to reported measurements (A) and what form of monitoring/reporting is required (B).

candidates.exact_span: Because State WQS for aluminum and copper were dissolved-based criteria, the linear partition coefficient for copper to convert dissolved copper concentration to total concentration is used to calculate the maximum daily effluent limitation. However, because a partition coefficient for aluminum is not available, the effluent limitation for total aluminum is based on the dissolved criteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of dissolved-versus-total conversion rules and the aluminum partition-coefficient exception could change the enforceable numeric effluent limits selected for copper and aluminum when comparing reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Three samples with hardness data were submitted and the average of these samples 187 mg/L was used for RP screening purposes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If applicable metal limits depend on hardness-based WQS calculations, treating 187 mg/L as the operative hardness value versus another value could change the calculated or selected enforceable limits used in compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The permit proposes to continue to include monitoring for hardness (CaCO3) for later RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether hardness monitoring is proposed as a continuing permit requirement affects whether monitoring for CaCO3 is established as required, not required, or unresolved for the evaluated period.

candidates.exact_span: Aluminum did show RP, however because the prescribed daily and 30 day average limit concentration (3.2 mg/l) is less stringent than the limit in the previous permit, the previous limit will be maintained at the request of NMED and to comply with antibacksliding requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of antibacksliding maintenance versus the proposed 3.2 mg/l daily and 30-day average values determines whether 0.75 mg/l or 3.2 mg/l is the operative enforceable limit for aluminum.

candidates.exact_span: Permit limit of 0.75 mg/l daily max was previously established for aluminum based on water quality standards. It is proposed that the permit limit of 0.75 mg/l be applied to the 30 day average.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 0.75 mg/l applies only as a daily maximum or also as the 30-day average limit changes which limit type is used when evaluating reported aluminum measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Because aluminum exhibited RP, daily and 30 day loadings of 0.78 lbs/day will be established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 0.78 lbs/day is an enforceable loading limit in addition to concentration limits affects which numeric compliance standard applies to aluminum discharges.

candidates.exact_span: Copper did not show RP, however permit limit of .0011 mg/l daily max was previously established for copper based on water quality standards and will be maintained in the draft permit. It is proposed that this limit be applied to the 30 day average as well.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Maintenance of the prior 0.0011 mg/l limit despite no RP, and its proposed extension to the 30-day average, affects which copper concentration limit is selected for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Because data is limited and discharge is infrequent, dissolved copper monitoring requirements will be maintained in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether dissolved copper monitoring is maintained because of data limitations and infrequent discharge affects whether copper monitoring was required (B) and how missing or infrequent results are classified when no ordinary numeric result is available (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee reported a non-detect result for Cadmium, however the testing submitted by the permittee did not satisfy SSM.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A non-detect paired with failure to satisfy SSM affects whether the absence of a numeric result is treated as documented no-data, inadequate evidence, or another missing-evidence state rather than an ordinary compliance result.

candidates.exact_span: As previously described the permittee has not discharged in over five years and is unable to obtain a sample to analyze at the appropriate detection level.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether prolonged no-discharge and inability to sample at the required detection level establishes that cadmium monitoring was not required, was required but unmet, or remains unresolved affects monitoring-obligation and missing-evidence classifications.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, the detection limit used by the permittee .002 mg/l was used as the effluent concentration value in RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Using the method detection limit as the effluent concentration for RP analysis bears on whether any numeric limit is derived from presumptive data (A) and whether reported non-detect evidence supports a documented no-data or presumptive-value state rather than a measured result (C).

candidates.exact_span: Because data is limited and based on presumptive values, Cadmium monitoring and reporting requirements will be added to the draft permit to obtain more current data for later RP analysis. Limits will not be prescribed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Addition of cadmium monitoring without prescribed limits affects whether cadmium has an enforceable numeric limit for comparison (A), whether cadmium monitoring is newly required (B), and how presumptive-value/no-limit situations are classified when results are missing or non-detect (C).

candidates.exact_span: EPA proposes to continue to maintain the oil and grease narrative "no visible sheen" limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A narrative sheen-based limit rather than a numeric concentration limit affects whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable or the limit must be treated as non-numeric/report-only for measurement exceedance analysis.
